units.title: False scanned starts cutting a scanned function
units.detail: From GitHub #43. On modern-GCC Emerald, 9 of 15 false starts sit inside true functions (6 in PokemonUseItemEffects, 0x08167cd1), cutting its extent so switch cases go unreached. Try: a scanned start can't cut a function whose analysis reached it by b or a far jump, or rank it down where a resolved jump lands. Check: just disc-pret pokeemerald_modern false-starts-inside goes down, code reached goes up, bars hold.

record.evidence: disc-pret pokeemerald_modern: false starts inside true functions 3 -> 2 (VBlankCB_Slice fixed; PokemonUseItemEffects already had none), precision 0.9993 -> 0.9994, recall 0.7776 -> 0.7777, code reached 712101 -> 712105. agbcc Emerald bar holds (0.9992/0.9555, unchanged), disc-agb unchanged, just check passes.

notes.text: Left: SetSelectedWordGroup+4 is a dead out-of-line copy (calls inlined) hit by a sound-data word. __aeabi_ddiv+0x19c is libgcc's ARM bleq Ldv_s, a bl used as a jump; returns mix sp 0/+16 so the far-jump rule misses it; ddiv itself is reached only by b from its veneer.

units.title: A branching helper in a caller's span taken as far jump
units.detail: From GitHub #48. The own-span bl rule (analyze_capped, crates/analysis/src/vsa/func.rs) treats a Thumb bl into its own reached span as a jump unless the target looks like a function; a helper ending bx lr but with a conditional branch or over 24 instructions becomes a false far jump. Skip targets whose probe returns balanced. Check: a unit test with such a helper; disc-agb, jt-score, both disc-pret hold.

record.evidence: Own-span bl rule now skips targets whose probe answers Bl::Balanced (every known return leaves sp at entry). New test branching_helper_in_the_span_is_a_call fails without the fix. jt-score 676/676, 584/617, far 548/548 and 726/732, 0 false; disc-agb 1.0/0.98, 1.0/0.86, 1.0/0.58; disc-pret 0.9992/0.9555 and 0.9994/0.7777, unchanged; just check passes.

units.title: Tiny agb functions reached only through pointers
units.detail: From GitHub #62. The agb sound ROM's last fallback entries are 6-8-byte Thumb functions (ldr r0,[pc]; bx lr getters, FnOnce::call_once shims) reached by bl to a bx rN stub with rN from data: 11 in the 18157 Hz ROM (0x08003871...0x08004f1d), 10 in 10512 Hz ROM. Let the pointer scan take very short pool-load + bx lr bodies, or feed fallback seeds back (decision 6). disc-agb precision 1.0 must hold; recall should rise.

record.evidence: Pointer scan scores constant getters (pool loads then bx lr) 2. disc-agb: agb sound ROM recall 0.857->0.969 (95/98), precision 1.0, others unchanged; disc-pret agbcc 0.9992/0.9555 unchanged, modern 12393->12407 found, 8 false starts as before. just check passes after merging main.

notes.text: Left: 0x08004ef9/0x08004f1d (vtable entries with a sub sp body, next to size/align words, not tiny) and 0x080051c1 (ldr r0,[r0]; b . : never returns, so validate rejects it). 3 of 98 in the agb sound ROM.

units.title: Remaining modern-GCC jump-table misses, if they cost
units.detail: From GitHub #23. 32 of 617 modern-GCC tables missed: mostly a narrowed index (bound on a zero-extended copy; needs backward refinement), one lost to the conservative frame rule. Misses only cost speed. First profile a modern-GCC game (Rogue, Imperium, moonbeam) for time in unresolved switches; if it's small, drop this with the numbers. Bars: jt-score 584/617 must not fall.

record.why: Profiled: misses cost almost nothing. Emerald Rogue recompiled (50 of 664 indirect jumps unresolved), 1800 and 5400 frames of menus: ROM-code fallback 0.1 points of running guest time (33-40 entry keys); moonbeam from its state, 1800 frames: 0% fallback (11 of 73 unresolved). jt-score untouched. Rogue's real cost is RAM code (37.7 points), filed separately.

units.title: Emerald Rogue's RAM code runs in the fallback (38% of time)
units.detail: Found profiling jump-table misses: Emerald Rogue recompiled, 5400 frames of menus, spends 37.8% of running guest cycles in the interpreter fallback, 37.7 points of it in RAM code; overlays 0 (decision 7 only finds agb's CpuSet/CpuFastSet copies). Find how pokeemerald-expansion copies code to IWRAM/EWRAM and recompile it as overlays. Building out/emerald-rogue needs a long job with --mem 14G (8G was killed).

record.evidence: Rogue (pokeemerald-expansion) copies its mixer by CpuSet through a swi;bx lr wrapper and patches its unrolled loop per channel. Now: wrapper copies found, per-block overlay guards, patched block versions compiled from a 1800-frame recompile-time interpreter run. Rogue 5400 frames of menus: fallback 37.8% to 2.2%, 42.0% compiled in RAM, frame hash+registers equal to interpreter. first-frame passes on iwram-rewrite (1 invalidation), agb sound ROM and gba-cart1 at 600; just check passes. Leftover 2.1 points filed as {unit:discovery/ram-code-misses}.

units.title: RAM code discovery misses: DMA copies, code on the stack
units.detail: After {unit:discovery/modern-iwram-code}, Rogue (5400 frames of menus) still spends 2.1 points of running guest time on RAM code in the fallback: ~1.7 the flash read code (agb_flash ReadFlash_Core, copied onto the stack by a CPU loop, run at 0x03007dd4, called from 0x0800ce93) and ~0.4 IntrMain (DmaCopy32 from ROM 0x0800025c to 0x03001930, 0x800 bytes). Decide if either is worth it; the same pattern is in vanilla Emerald. Measure: build out/emerald-rogue as a long job with --mem 14G.

record.evidence: IntrMain (DMA copy): worth it, done. gbaa-recompile's 1800-frame run now finds IWRAM code outside known copies, locates its bytes in ROM and compiles it as overlays (codegen/src/seen.rs). Stack code (ReadFlash_Core): not worth it, left interpreted: its address moves with call depth (d28/d58 at recompile, dd4 later) and it is a one-time save read at boot. Rogue 5400 frames, same runtime: RAM-code fallback 1.9 -> 1.7 points, fallback 11.47M -> 10.43M cycles; hash 317f1f5fd5f7b3ba equal to interpreter. first-frame iwram-rewrite passes; just check passes.

notes.text: just run-recompiled passes its args unquoted ({{args}}), so a ROM path with a space (Emerald Rogue.gba) splits; ran target/recompiled/release/gbaa-emerald-rogue directly. Wait states doubled Rogue's running cycles: old 5400-frame cycle lines aren't comparable.

units.title: Modern GCC's far-jump bl into a caller's fragment

notes.text: From {unit:native/entry-read-masking}: moonbeam's 0x0801a080 (bl from 0x08019886, 0x0801aa16...), Rogue 0x0820c629, Imperium 0x0821e331 are fragments of a huge function reached by bl that never returns; far_jumps misses them, so the lift calls them with r4-r12 zeroed (hard entry reads).

units.title: Cold-block rule: variadic neighbours and stale lead-ins
units.detail: From the review of {unit:discovery/gcc-far-jump-bl} (PR 11). analysis::vsa::func, the rule that a bl to a never-returning block right after a function's code is a jump: (1) a real never-returning function placed right after its caller whose start is_push_lr doesn't take for a prologue is taken for a block: a variadic one (push {r0-r3}; push {r4, lr}: is_push_lr stops at the first push), one with no saves, a lone 'b .'. The code runs the same, but the function start is lost if nothing else calls it; no corpus case seen (Rogue's 'falls and jumps into another function's entry' went 72 to 65). (2) is_push_lr decodes up to 9 instructions at a target that FuncResult::reads doesn't record, so new data over a callee's lead-in doesn't redo the caller. Done: a test each, the rule fixed or the limit written in the doc comment, disc-* and jt-score bars held, holes-all with no hard count higher.
